#### 成本

| 阶段 | 现金与资源成本 | 人工与时间投入 | 已知条件与未知项 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 首次使用 | 包/Skill与模型接入；金额未知 | 核技能加载、配置和diff范围 | DSH真实运行未验 |
| 持续使用 | 指南上下文和模型调用；token/金额未知 | 核出处、后果和修法 | 无准确率/净节时对照 |
| 失败恢复 | 重跑与人工复核资源 | 丢弃误报、恢复代码/历史文件 | review外修复模式另有写入风险 |
先用小diff的review模式，保留人工评审与静态lint；不要凭健康分自动改代码或合并。见[Q04](#research-q04)。

#### 效果

| 效果项 | 当前证据支持 | 尚不能确定 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 诊断一致结构 | Skill要求四段发现链 | 模型遵守与发现正确率 |
| DSH加载 | provider与资源目录接线 | 实际宿主读取/触发 |
| 评分 | 严重性扣分规则 | 真实代码质量与跨项目可比性 |
共享指南与每Skill resourceBase避免复制分叉，frontmatter错误显式失败便于维护；模型遵守仍无强制执行门槛，移植需验技能资源读取，见[Q02](#research-q02)。
把既有工程书目与风险分类组织成症状—出处—后果—修法的评审流程，便于人工核对，不是新静态分析器。见[Q01](#research-q01)。

# brooks-lint > 以十二本工程经典的风险框架组织代码、架构和测试评审，提供六种 Agent Skills 模式。 ## 研究范围 - **仓库**：[hyhmrright/brooks-lint](https://github.com/hyhmrright/brooks-lint) - **版本号**：1.9.1（[固定提交 15fa2d49877969f65a25b9f05897cd72fae32d33](https://github.com/hyhmrright/brooks-lint/tree/15fa2d49877969f65a25b9f05897cd72fae32d33)） - **版本日期**：2026-10-26（固定提交日期，北京时间；不是包发布日期） ## 研究问题与完整回答 **插件研究总目标**：核查书目评审框架相对自写提示的增量、DSH技能加载及评估边界 ### Q01 · 经典书目驱动的评审Skill为谁提供什么增量？ **研究主题**：场景与需求、贡献与相对优势 #### 完整回答 目标用户是已经用模型做PR评审、希望结构性问题能说清症状、原则出处、后果和修法的开发者。合格发现必须对应具体代码和后果，可由评审人接受或驳回，不是仅产生健康分。相对自己写“注意可维护性”的提示，它提供生产/测试风险分类、模式化流程和共享例外/取舍材料；相对ESLint等确定性规则，它依赖模型理解架构和领域，不替代语法/规则lint。作者十二书目的来源映射是对既有工程思想的组织，不能算新理论，也不能以引文增加证明发现正确。其可借鉴贡献是让建议必须经过诊断并以统一证据链交付。 #### 证据与依据 **依据 1 · 源码核查**：[skills/brooks-review/SKILL.md:22-40](https://github.com/hyhmrright/brooks-lint/blob/15fa2d49877969f65a25b9f05897cd72fae32d33/skills/brooks-review/SKILL.md#L22-L40) 先读共享框架、来源与风险再完成诊断

Valid codes: `R1` `R2` `R3` `R4` `R5` `R6` `T1` `T2` `T3` `T4` `T5` `T6` **`severity`** — override the severity of a specific risk for this project. Valid values: `critical` `warning` `suggestion` Example: `R1: suggestion` means every R1 finding is downgraded to Suggestion regardless of what the guide says. **`ignore`** — list of glob patterns. Files matching any pattern are excluded from analysis. Findings that arise solely from ignored files are omitted. Common entries: `**/*.generated.*`, `**/vendor/**`, `**/migrations/**` **`focus`** — non-empty list of risk codes to evaluate; all others are skipped. Adding an AI assistant doesn't fix cognitive overload or domain model distortion; generating more code increases change propagation and knowledge duplication; moving faster makes accidental complexity and dependency disorder more dangerous. ## Project Structure Every skill is one `SKILL.md` (trigger + process skeleton) plus its own guide: ``` brooks-lint/ ├── .claude-plugin/ · .codex-plugin/ # plugin metadata per platform ├── skills/ │ ├── _shared/ # common.md (Iron Law, config, report template, Health Score) │ │ # source-coverage.md · decay-risks.md (R1–R6) │ │ # test-decay-risks.md (T1–T6) · remedy-guide.md · custom-risks-guide.md │ ├── brooks-review/ # Mode 1: PR Review → pr-review-guide.md │ ├── brooks-audit/ # Mode 2: Architecture Audit → architecture-guide.md, onboarding-guide.md │ ├── brooks-debt/ # Mode 3: Tech Debt → debt-guide.md │ ├── brooks-test/ # Mode 4: Test Quality → test-guide.md │ ├── brooks-health/ # Mode 5: Health Dashboard → health-guide.md │ └── brooks-sweep/ # Mode 6: Full Sweep → sweep-guide.md ├── hooks/ # SessionStart hook ├── commands/ # short-form command wrappers (auto-installed by the hook) ├── evals/ # 58-scenario eval suite + frozen parser-fidelity corpus └── assets/ # logo, banner, demo ``` ## CI/CD Integration Automate brooks-lint on every PR using the GitHub Action: ```yaml # .github/workflows/brooks-lint.yml name: Brooks-Lint PR Review on: pull_request: types: [opened, synchronize, reopened] jobs: brooks-lint: runs-on: ubuntu-latest permissions: pull-requests: write steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v7 with: fetch-depth: 0 - uses: hyhmrright/brooks-lint/.github/actions/brooks-lint@v1.9.1 with: mode: review anthropic-api-key: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }} fail-below: 70 ``` See [`docs/github-action-example.yml`](docs/github-action-example.yml) for the full template. The action posts the review as a PR comment and optionally fails the check if the Health Score drops below a threshold. If `.brooks-lint-history.json` is committed to your repo, the comment also includes a trend delta (e.g., "85 → 82 (−3) over last 3 runs"). **`mode: sweep` in CI reports but never applies fixes.** The action makes a single tool-less API call, so Full Sweep's consent gate (Step 0), its in-place file edits, and its iteration loop cannot run — the Fix Log and Iteration History sections come back empty, and `sweep.max_iterations` from `.brooks-lint.yaml` is inert here. What you get is a description of a sweep, not a sweep. For fixes that actually land, run `/brooks-sweep` interactively in a harness that has file tools and can answer the Step 0 consent prompt. The five read-only modes — `review`, `audit`, `debt`, `test`, `health` — behave in CI exactly as they do locally. **Quality gates and Code Scanning.** Beyond `fail-below`, the action exposes: ```yaml with: mode: review anthropic-api-key: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }} fail-on: critical # fail on any Critical finding (none | warning | critical) fail-on-regression: true # fail if the Health Score dropped vs the last run sarif-file: brooks-lint.sarif # also upload findings to GitHub Code Scanning ``` `fail-on-regression` reads `.brooks-lint-history.json`, so commit that file to enforce "no new regressions". Setting `sarif-file` makes findings appear inline on the PR's **Files changed** tab and requires `security-events: write` permission on the job. **Project config in CI.** The action applies your `.brooks-lint.yaml` — `strictness`, `disable`, `focus`, `severity`, `ignore`, `custom_risks` — and reads it **from the base branch**, not from the PR's checkout. A pull request therefore cannot weaken the policy that reviews it: a diff that disables every risk would otherwise score 100 and sail through `fail-below` before anyone approved the config change. A config a PR adds for the first time takes effect once merged, for the same reason. The report's `Config:` line names the provenance it used (e.g. `applied from base (main)`). This needs the base object in the clone, which is why the template checks out with `fetch-depth: 0`; in a PR, missing base refs stop the action with an error instructing you to use `fetch-depth: 0`. It never falls back to the PR's policy. Outside PRs (including local runs), unavailable base refs fall back to the working-tree config with an explicit provenance note. Set `config-ref: head` to use the PR's own copy instead — appropriate when `.brooks-lint.yaml` is CODEOWNERS-protected and config changes should take effect in the PR that makes them: ```yaml with: mode: review anthropic-api-key: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }} config-ref: base # base (default) | head ``` **Custom API endpoint.** `api-base-url` points the action at any Anthropic-compatible `/v1/messages` endpoint — a self-hosted proxy, an LLM gateway, a regional mirror — instead of `api.anthropic.com`. Pass that endpoint's key as `anthropic-api-key` and the model id it expects as `model`: ```yaml with: mode: review api-base-url: https://your-gateway.example.com anthropic-api-key: ${{ secrets.GATEWAY_API_KEY }} model: gateway-model-id ``` brooks-lint sends your diff to whatever host you name here, so only point it at one you trust with your source. Running `scripts/ci-review.mjs` yourself needs no flag at all — the Anthropic SDK reads `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` directly. **Claude on Amazon Bedrock.** Bedrock serves the [Anthropic Messages API](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/inference-messages-api.html) natively, so no new client is needed: point `api-base-url` (action `v1.6.0`+) at `https://bedrock-runtime.{region}.amazonaws.com/anthropic` and pass a short-term [Bedrock API key](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/api-keys.html) as `anthropic-api-key` — minted inside the job from an OIDC-assumed role, so no long-lived key sits in a secret. [`docs/github-action-example.yml`](docs/github-action-example.yml) carries the full wiring as commented steps: role assumption, token minting, model ids, the IAM permissions needed, and the `bedrock-mantle` alternative. The trust note above still applies — with Bedrock the diff goes to your own AWS account, in the Region you name. **This path cannot review pull requests from forks.** GitHub grants a forked `pull_request` run neither repository secrets nor `id-token: write`, so there is no OIDC token to exchange for the role and no stored key to fall back on. Fork coverage needs a different trigger (`pull_request_target`, with all the care that running against untrusted branches demands) or a different key source. **Output ceiling.** `max-tokens: 8192` raises the report's output ceiling (default 4096). A long `sweep` or `health` report can hit that ceiling, and truncation fails in the wrong direction: the findings that were cut off are never counted, so the Health Score comes back *higher* and a `fail-below` gate can pass a run it should have failed. You do not have to notice that yourself: a run whose report was cut off carries a `::warning::` annotation, repeats the warning in the PR comment, and sets `"truncated": true` in `brooks-lint-report.json` — raise `max-tokens` and re-run. The run is not failed over it. **Cost:** ~$0.05–0.15 per PR run depending on diff size and model.
